papers.title: Longitudinal Exploratory Analysis of Salivary Microbiota Profiles in Patients with Oral Squamous Cell Carcinoma Before and After Surgery: A Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Salivary microbiome profiling may represent a promising non-invasive approach for characterizing OSCC-associated microbial patterns and longitudinal microbiome dynamics during patient management. This exploratory pilot study aimed to longitudinally assess salivary microbiota profiles in patients with oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) before and after tumor resection using Oxford Nanopore Technology. Unstimulated saliva samples were collected from 16 patients with OSCC at two time points (before and after tumor resection) and from 10 OSCC-free reference subjects. Microbial DNA was extracted u
papers.summary: This pilot study used Oxford Nanopore Technology to longitudinally profile salivary microbiota in 16 oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) patients before and after tumor resection, comparing them to 10 healthy controls. The findings suggest that salivary microbiome profiles may shift after surgery, highlighting the potential of non-invasive salivary sampling for monitoring microbial dynamics in OSCC management.

papers.title: Clinical Improvement and Taxonomic-Functional Gut Microbiome Remodeling After Six Months of Multi-Strain Synbiotic Supplementation in Mexican Children with Autism Spectrum Disorder.
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Gut dysbiosis in children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has been associated with alterations in microbial ecology and metabolic function that may contribute to gastrointestinal dysfunction and the severity of clinical manifestations. Synbiotic and probiotic supplementation has emerged as a promising microbiome-targeted strategy for ASD; however, its effects on gut microbiome composition, functional potential, and clinical outcomes remain incompletely understood. We conducted a longitudinal study of Mexican children diagnosed with ASD to analyze changes in the compo
papers.summary: This longitudinal study of Mexican children with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) found that six months of multi-strain synbiotic supplementation led to clinical improvement and significant remodeling of the gut microbiome, including changes in both taxonomic composition and functional potential. The results support the potential of synbiotics as a microbiome-targeted intervention for ASD, though further research is needed to confirm causality and long-term effects.

papers.title: Effects of Non-Surgical Periodontal Therapy on Dental Plaque Microbiome.
papers.abstract: Periodontitis, a chronic inflammatory disease affecting approximately 40% of U.S. adults aged 30 years and older, is characterized by dysbiosis of the dental plaque microbiome. However, although scaling and root planing (SRP) is the cornerstone of periodontal treatment, its effects on the taxonomic composition and functional potential of the dental plaque microbiome remain incompletely understood. In this study, we used whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing to characterize taxonomic composition and functional potential in dental plaque microbiomes collected from 39 patients with Stage II or III
papers.summary: This study uses whole-metagenome shotgun sequencing to examine how non-surgical periodontal therapy (scaling and root planing) alters the dental plaque microbiome in patients with periodontitis. The findings reveal changes in taxonomic composition and functional potential, providing insights into the microbial shifts associated with treatment.

papers.title: Primer-Less Species Identification Throughout Fungal (Tuber magnatum), Plant (Corylus avellana) and Animal (Eisenia fetida) Kingdoms by Direct RNA Sequencing.
papers.abstract: Accurate species identification is essential for biodiversity studies, ecological monitoring, and biosecurity, but current molecular approaches rely on PCR amplification, which requires universal primers. Here, we evaluated the possibility of primer-free species identification via direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) by using Oxford Nanopore Technology (ONT). Total RNA isolated from three major eukaryotic kingdoms-fungal (Tuber magnatum Picco 1788), plant (Corylus avellana L. 1753), and animal (Eisenia fetida Savigny 1826) specimens-was sequenced without reverse transcription and PCR amplification
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that direct RNA sequencing (dRNA-seq) using Oxford Nanopore Technology can identify species across three eukaryotic kingdoms (fungi, plant, animal) without the need for PCR amplification or universal primers. By sequencing total RNA directly from Tuber magnatum, Corylus avellana, and Eisenia fetida, the authors show that primer-free species identification is feasible, potentially simplifying biodiversity and biosecurity workflows.

papers.title: Microbial metabolite-driven mechanisms linking the gut microbiome to atherosclerosis: multi-omic and translational perspectives.
papers.abstract: Atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease remains the leading cause of mortality worldwide, and a substantial residual risk persists despite optimal management of traditional risk factors. Increasing evidence implicates the gut microbiome as a mechanistic contributor to atherogenesis, not merely through taxonomic shifts but via the production of bioactive microbial metabolites that link diet, microbial metabolism, and host vascular biology. These metabolites have emerged as central effectors of the gut-artery axis, influencing intestinal barrier integrity, systemic immunity, lipid handling, and t
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current evidence on how gut microbiome-derived metabolites contribute to atherosclerosis, highlighting the gut-artery axis and its effects on intestinal barrier function, immunity, and lipid metabolism. It emphasizes multi-omic and translational approaches to uncover mechanistic links and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Gut microbiome signatures during acute infection are associated with long COVID.
papers.abstract: Long COVID (LC) manifests in 10%-30% of non-hospitalized individuals post-SARS-CoV-2 infection, leading to significant morbidity. The predictive role of gut microbiome composition during acute infection in the development of LC is not well understood, partly because of the heterogeneous nature of the disease.
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiome composition during acute SARS-CoV-2 infection can predict the development of long COVID. The findings suggest that specific gut microbiome signatures are associated with long COVID, potentially offering early biomarkers for identifying at-risk individuals.

papers.title: Environmental selection shapes the ecological cascade of biofilm assembly and functional gene abundance in sandstone weathering.
papers.abstract: Microorganisms are pivotal agents in the process of sandstone weathering; nevertheless, the ecological mechanisms that govern their transition from mere colonization to sustained weathering activity remain ambiguous. This study systematically elucidated microbe-mediated weathering mechanisms through amplicon and metagenomic sequencing of bacteria, fungi, and archaea across a sandstone weathering sequence-from original unweathered sandstone (OS), biofilm-covered sandstone (BS), to weathered sandstone (WS). The findings indicate that microbial communities undergo associations across a weathering
papers.summary: This study uses amplicon and metagenomic sequencing to show that as sandstone weathers, microbial communities shift from simple colonization to active weathering, with environmental selection shaping biofilm assembly and functional gene abundance. The findings reveal a clear ecological cascade linking community composition to weathering activity.

papers.title: Metagenomic analysis of commensal small mammal samples from an international cargo shipping area, Bangkok Port, reveals potential zoonotic pathogens and implications for One Health surveillance.
papers.abstract: Commensal small mammals, such as rats and shrews, are recognized reservoirs for numerous zoonotic pathogens; however, their role in pathogen circulation at transport hubs remains underexplored. This study employs shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial communities and assess zoonotic potential in tissue samples from commensal small mammals captured at Bangkok Port, an international cargo shipping hub in Thailand between June and August 2025. Following host read depletion, taxonomic profiling was performed to identify bacterial taxa of public health relevance, including sequenc
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to characterize microbial communities in commensal small mammals (rats and shrews) captured at Bangkok Port, an international shipping hub, and identified potential zoonotic pathogens. The findings highlight the role of transport hubs in pathogen circulation and underscore the importance of One Health surveillance at such interfaces.

papers.title: Large language models enhance annotation of enzymes in metagenomes.
papers.abstract: Metagenomic data have notable biological potential, but their functional interpretation is frequently impeded by incomplete protein function annotations. Accurate enzyme annotation is essential for elucidating the metabolic capabilities of microbial communities within metagenomic datasets. To address this challenge, we developed FEDKEA, an enzyme annotation tool leveraging protein language models, and provided a web platform for its use. In addition, we designed a user-friendly, FEDKEA-based metagenomic pipeline, MEnzMap, which encompasses the entire analysis workflow-from raw data quality con
papers.summary: The authors developed FEDKEA, an enzyme annotation tool that uses protein language models to improve functional annotation of metagenomic data, along with a web platform and a companion pipeline called MEnzMap for end-to-end metagenomic analysis. This approach addresses the common problem of incomplete enzyme annotations in metagenomes, potentially enabling better understanding of microbial metabolic capabilities.

papers.title: The use of multi-species probiotic-derived vesicles to encapsulate luteolin for preventing colitis in a mouse model.
papers.abstract: Probiotic-derived membrane vesicles (MVs) offer advantages over live probiotics, including lower immunogenicity and enhanced bioavailability of dietary compounds. However, their composition and function depend on culture conditions. In this study, MVs from a single probiotic strain (S-MVs) were compared with those from co-cultured multi-species probiotics (M-MVs). M-MVs showed superior radical scavenging ability due to characteristic antioxidant proteins. Luteolin (Lut), a hydrophobic flavonoid, was loaded into M-MVs to generate Lut-MVs. Compared with Lut or M-MVs alone, Lut-MVs had enhanced w
papers.summary: This study demonstrates that membrane vesicles derived from co-cultured multi-species probiotics (M-MVs) have superior antioxidant properties compared to single-strain vesicles, and can effectively encapsulate the hydrophobic flavonoid luteolin. The resulting luteolin-loaded vesicles (Lut-MVs) showed enhanced efficacy in preventing colitis in a mouse model, suggesting a promising strategy for using probiotic-derived vesicles as drug delivery vehicles for inflammatory bowel disease.

papers.title: AI-Guided Computational Design of Synthetic Microbiota for Next-Generation Immunomodulatory Applications.
papers.abstract: The growing recognition of the human microbiome as a key regulator of immune homeostasis has accelerated the application of computational intelligence for microbiome-driven disease understanding and therapeutic design. However, existing microbiome studies largely rely on classical machine learning or shallow deep learning models that fail to capture higher-order microbial interactions, multimodal functional dependencies, and immune feasibility constraints simultaneously. Moreover, most approaches lack biological constraint enforcement, leading to predictions that may be statistically accurate
papers.summary: This review discusses the use of AI-guided computational design for synthetic microbiota aimed at immunomodulatory applications, highlighting the limitations of current machine learning and shallow deep learning models in capturing complex microbial interactions and biological constraints. It emphasizes the need for more advanced computational approaches to design effective microbiome-based therapies.

papers.title: First-void urine and cervicovaginal brushes for vaginal microbiome profiling: a proof-of-concept study.
papers.abstract: The human vaginal microbiome is a cornerstone of female reproductive health, influencing susceptibility to vaginal conditions, pregnancy complications, and urogenital infections. Understanding this microbiome is critical for advancing preventive, diagnostic, and therapeutic interventions, yet its intimate and dynamic nature poses challenges for accurate, representative, and more inclusive sampling methods. This proof-of-concept study evaluated the performance of first-void urine (FVU) samples and cervicovaginal brushes for vaginal microbiome profiling relative to vaginal swabs. FVU refers to t
papers.summary: This proof-of-concept study evaluates first-void urine (FVU) and cervicovaginal brushes as alternative sampling methods for vaginal microbiome profiling compared to standard vaginal swabs. The findings suggest that FVU and brushes can provide representative microbiome data, potentially enabling more inclusive and less invasive sampling for vaginal health research.

papers.title: A Tri-Source Microbiome Dataset from Human Sleep Environments: Saliva, Pillow Dust, and Bedroom Air.
papers.abstract: Despite the established importance of the human microbiome in health, the integrated microbial exposures occurring within the sleep environment remain poorly understood. Sleep represents a critical period of prolonged exposure to indoor microbial reservoirs, yet no study has simultaneously examined the connectivity between environmental sources and the human oral microbiome. We present a novel, tri-source microbiome dataset characterizing microbial communities from co-located saliva, pillow dust, and bedroom air collected from healthy participants in real-world sleep environments. Samples were
papers.summary: This paper introduces a new dataset that simultaneously profiles microbial communities from human saliva, pillow dust, and bedroom air in real-world sleep environments, addressing a gap in understanding integrated microbial exposures during sleep. The tri-source design enables exploration of connections between environmental reservoirs and the human oral microbiome, providing a resource for future studies on sleep-environment health impacts.

papers.title: Joint-RPCA: domain-aware multi-omics integration for systems microbiology.
papers.abstract: Integrating multi-omics data is essential for microbiome research, as microbial communities are shaped by and respond to interdependent processes, including taxonomic composition, metabolite production and utilization, and gene expression. However, accurately capturing ecosystem-wide patterns across these modalities is statistically challenging due to differences in scale, sparsity, and compositionality. While a growing number of multi-omics methods have emerged, they differ in their mathematical objectives and modeling assumptions, which in turn shape how biological patterns are represented a
papers.summary: This paper introduces Joint-RPCA, a domain-aware multi-omics integration method for microbiome data that addresses challenges like scale differences, sparsity, and compositionality. It provides a statistically robust framework to capture ecosystem-wide patterns across taxonomic, metabolomic, and transcriptomic modalities, offering a new tool for systems microbiology.

papers.title: Promises and Pitfalls of Long-Read Sequencing for Resolving Microbial Complexity.
papers.abstract: Long-read sequencing (LRS) has driven a transition in microbial genomics, overcoming the assembly fragmentation inherent to short-read sequencing. This review elucidates the impact of LRS across isolate genomics, metagenomics, and multi-omics domains. By spanning extensive repetitive regions, LRS facilitates the reconstruction of circular chromosomes and precisely resolves mobile genetic elements (MGEs). In metagenomics, LRS enables strain-level resolution, the recovery of circular metagenome-assembled genomes, and the precise localization of MGEs within host replicons. Furthermore, the single
papers.summary: This review discusses how long-read sequencing has transformed microbial genomics by overcoming short-read assembly limitations, enabling complete circular genomes and precise resolution of mobile genetic elements. It highlights applications in isolate genomics, metagenomics, and multi-omics, while also addressing current pitfalls and challenges.

papers.title: Fantastic Microbes and Where to Find Them: evaluating learning-by-doing outcomes in a crowdfunded metagenomics workshop.
papers.abstract: Metagenomics offers a powerful framework for authentic, interdisciplinary learning, yet it remains underrepresented in undergraduate education due to technical and infrastructural barriers. We hypothesized that a research-based, learning-by-doing metagenomics workshop supported by accessible bioinformatics tools could enhance students' perceived skills, self-efficacy, and conceptual understanding of metagenomic analysis. To test this hypothesis, we designed and evaluated a hybrid hands-on workshop in which undergraduate and postgraduate students analyzed real environmental shotgun metagenomic
papers.summary: This paper evaluates a crowdfunded, hands-on metagenomics workshop for undergraduate and postgraduate students, finding that a learning-by-doing approach with accessible bioinformatics tools improved students' perceived skills, self-efficacy, and conceptual understanding of metagenomic analysis. The study supports the feasibility of integrating authentic metagenomics research into university curricula despite technical and infrastructural barriers.

papers.title: Prospective associations of tea consumption with skeletal muscle mass and strength: Insights from the gut microbiome and proteomics.
papers.abstract: Tea consumption may be associated with skeletal muscle health, but longitudinal evidence based on repeated assessments remains limited. We examined the associations of tea intake and serum biomarkers with repeated skeletal muscle measures and explored whether these associations might be partly explained by multi-omics features. In this prospective cohort, 3408 adults were followed for approximately 12 years. Skeletal muscle mass was measured by dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry, handgrip strength by digital dynamometry, gut microbial taxonomic and functional profiles by shotgun metagenomic sequ
papers.summary: This prospective cohort study of 3,408 adults followed for ~12 years found that tea consumption is associated with better skeletal muscle mass and strength over time, and suggests that gut microbiome composition and serum proteomics may partly mediate these protective effects. The findings provide longitudinal evidence linking tea intake to muscle health and highlight potential multi-omics pathways.

papers.title: Environmental filtering shapes biosynthetic potential and resistome of antarctic microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Environmental filtering is a major driver of microbial community assembly in Antarctic ecosystems, yet its influence on biosynthetic potential and antimicrobial resistance remains poorly understood. Here, we analyzed 319 medium- to high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) recovered from four Antarctic sites (Whalers Bay, Crater Lake, Fumarole Bay, and Hannah Point) to investigate the relationship between geochemical gradients, biosynthetic gene clusters (BGCs), and antimicrobial resistance genes (ARGs). Integrating genome-resolved metagenomics, biosynthetic mining, resistome profiling,
papers.summary: This study analyzed 319 metagenome-assembled genomes from four Antarctic sites to show that environmental filtering, driven by geochemical gradients, shapes both the biosynthetic potential (biosynthetic gene clusters) and the resistome (antimicrobial resistance genes) of Antarctic microbiomes. The findings reveal that local environmental conditions, rather than phylogenetic relatedness alone, are key determinants of the distribution of these functional traits, providing insights into microbial adaptation in extreme environments.

papers.title: Natural Products for Depression: Preclinical Insights into Microbiota-Gut-Brain Axis Modulation and Pharmacological Potential.
papers.abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis (MGBA) is progressively associated with the pathophysiology of depression. This analysis consolidates existing preclinical findings on MGBA mechanisms associated with depression and assesses natural-product therapies through three key metabolite-related pathways: bile acid-responsive signaling via the farnesoid X receptor, G protein-coupled bile acid receptor 1, vitamin D receptor, and pregnane X receptor; metabolites from the kynurenine pathway and their connection to N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor signaling; and microbial indole-aryl hydrocarbon receptor signalin
papers.summary: This review consolidates preclinical evidence linking the microbiota-gut-brain axis to depression and evaluates natural-product therapies that act through three key metabolite pathways: bile acid signaling, kynurenine pathway metabolites, and microbial indole-aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling. It highlights the pharmacological potential of natural products in modulating these pathways for depression treatment.

papers.title: Modeling microbiome modulation of tumor metabolic networks to predict synergistic therapies.
papers.abstract: Differences in microbiome composition profoundly influence drug response, yet methods to model the metabolic impact of microbes on host cells and therapeutics remain limited. We present a microbiome-aware computational framework combining machine learning and genome-scale metabolic models to predict combination therapies for colorectal cancer (CRC) in the presence of Fusobacterium nucleatum (Fn) and other pathogenic, probiotic, and commensal microbes. The model learned predictive metabolic flux signatures from 6,514 drug combination profiles in CRC cell lines and predicted synergistic drug com
papers.summary: This paper presents a computational framework that integrates machine learning with genome-scale metabolic models to predict how the microbiome influences drug responses in colorectal cancer. The model identifies metabolic flux signatures from thousands of drug combination profiles and predicts synergistic therapies in the presence of specific microbes like Fusobacterium nucleatum, offering a new approach to microbiome-aware cancer treatment design.

papers.title: Blood and gut virome remodeling in gastric cancer: Anellovirus expansion and novel virus discovery.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer (GC) is a prevalent malignancy worldwide, yet effective early diagnostic tools remain lacking, and the role of the virome, a key component of the tumor microenvironment, in GC progression is largely unknown. This study aimed to characterize the virome landscapes in peripheral blood and feces of GC patients versus healthy controls, and to identify viral signatures associated with GC onset and metastasis. We performed viral metagenomic sequencing on pooled libraries from 100 GC patients (45 non-metastatic, 55 metastatic) and 50 healthy controls, followed by taxonomic annotation, d
papers.summary: This study characterizes the blood and gut virome in gastric cancer patients, revealing an expansion of anelloviruses and identifying novel viruses associated with cancer onset and metastasis. These findings suggest that virome composition could serve as a potential biomarker for gastric cancer.

papers.title: Dental wastewater reveals a hidden reservoir of oral bacteriophage diversity.
papers.abstract: Bacteriophages (phages) are being explored as alternatives or complements to antibiotics because of their ability to selectively kill bacterial pathogens. However, phages that infect many oral bacteria remain undiscovered. Here, we discovered that dental wastewater harbors previously underexplored phage diversity. Viral particles concentrated from dental wastewater displayed diverse morphologies, including abundant filamentous phage-like particles. Deep long-read metagenomic sequencing of concentrated viral particles generated 7.4 billion bases of sequence data and yielded 255 medium- to high-
papers.summary: This study discovered that dental wastewater contains a previously unexplored reservoir of diverse bacteriophages, including many filamentous phage-like particles. Using deep long-read metagenomic sequencing, the authors generated 7.4 billion bases of sequence data and assembled 255 medium- to high-quality phage genomes, significantly expanding the known diversity of oral phages.

papers.title: Drought stress adaptation in Ficus carica L.: Modulation of ROS scavenging, nitrogen uptake, and rhizosphere bacterial community assembly and functions.
papers.abstract: Rhizosphere microorganisms are crucial for plant drought resistance; however, their response to drought stress in fig plants remains poorly understood. In this study, potted 'BoJi Red' fig plants were utilized to systematically investigate drought-induced changes in the structure, assembly processes, and functional potential of rhizosphere bacterial communities. The results showed that drought significantly inhibited fig growth, photosynthesis, and nitrogen uptake, while increasing reactive oxygen species (ROS) content and antioxidant enzyme activities, although these enzyme activities decline
papers.summary: This study examines how drought stress affects fig plants and their rhizosphere bacterial communities, revealing that drought inhibits growth and nitrogen uptake while altering bacterial community assembly and functions. The findings suggest that rhizosphere microorganisms play a role in fig drought adaptation, potentially informing strategies to improve crop resilience.

papers.title: Exploring the hypothetical role of Bacteroides species in depression progression: insights from metagenomic analysis.
papers.abstract: Depression, a psychiatric disorder with significant morbidity and mortality, has a complex etiology. Recent advances in microbiome research have highlighted the potential role of fecal microbiota in depression pathogenesis. This study utilized shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare the fecal microbiota of 28 depression patients and 26 healthy individuals. Significant differences in fecal microbiota composition were observed between the two groups. We generated 350 non-redundant high-quality metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs) by binning and conducted comparisons between the depression and c
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomic sequencing to compare gut microbiota between depression patients and healthy controls, identifying compositional differences and generating 350 metagenome-assembled genomes (MAGs). The findings suggest a potential role for Bacteroides species in depression progression, offering insights into the gut-brain axis.

papers.title: Sustainable Protein Transitions: A Comprehensive Review of Insect Meal in Broiler Diets-Nutritional Value, Immunomodulatory Effects, Gut Health Interactions, and Future Perspectives.
papers.abstract: Broiler production keeps intensifying, and the environmental cost of the protein sources that feed it, principally soybean meal and fishmeal, has become harder to justify. Insect meal, derived chiefly from black soldier fly larvae (Hermetia illucens), yellow mealworm (Tenebrio molitor), and housefly larvae (Musca domestica), has emerged as a candidate able to address nutritional, immunological, and ecological goals at once. This review evaluates the evidence on the nutritional composition, digestibility, growth performance, immunomodulatory mechanisms, and gut health effects of insect meal in
papers.summary: This review examines the potential of insect meal as a sustainable protein source for broiler chickens, focusing on its nutritional value, effects on growth, immune function, and gut health. It concludes that insect meal, particularly from black soldier fly larvae, can serve as a viable alternative to soybean and fishmeal, though further research is needed to optimize its use.

papers.title: Convergent Gut Microbiome Remodeling Across Ischemic Stroke, Myocardial Infarction, and Longevity Reveals a Shared Ecological Signature of Aging and Disease.
papers.abstract: Gut microbiota dysbiosis has been associated with ischemic stroke (IS), myocardial infarction (MI), and aging, but whether these contexts share reproducible microbial features remains unclear. We conducted an exploratory and hypothesis-generating descriptive study of genus-level microbiota patterns across an internal IS cohort and publicly available external IS, MI, and age-stratified or longevity-associated datasets. Analyses were performed within predefined age strata and interpreted cautiously because of the small internal cohort, cross-cohort heterogeneity, and the absence of direct metabo
papers.summary: This study investigates whether gut microbiome changes are shared across ischemic stroke, myocardial infarction, and aging. By analyzing internal and public datasets, the authors find a convergent ecological signature of dysbiosis common to these conditions, suggesting a shared microbial pattern linked to aging and disease. The findings are exploratory due to small cohort sizes and cross-study heterogeneity.

papers.title: Alcohol Consumption and Gut Microbiota-Derived Metabolites in Primates: A Systematic Review.
papers.abstract: Alcohol consumption has been increasingly associated with alterations in the gut microbiota and its metabolic activity; however, evidence regarding microbiota-derived metabolites remains fragmented. This systematic review aimed to synthesize current evidence on the effects of alcohol consumption on gut microbiota-derived metabolites in humans and non-human primates. The review was conducted according to Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines and included studies published between 2012 and 2026. Searches were performed in PubMed, Web of Science, S
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesizes current evidence on how alcohol consumption affects gut microbiota-derived metabolites in humans and non-human primates, following PRISMA guidelines and covering studies from 2012 to 2026. It highlights fragmented evidence and aims to consolidate findings on alcohol-induced metabolic changes in the gut microbiome.

papers.title: Optimized Controlled-Release Fertilization Improves Productivity and Reshapes the Rhizosphere Microbiome in Lei Bamboo: A Metagenomic Assessment.
papers.abstract: Intensive nitrogen fertilization in Lei bamboo (Phyllostachys praecox) plantations has increased productivity but has also reduced nitrogen-use efficiency (NUE), accelerated nutrient losses, and contributed to soil degradation. How nutrient-release strategies influence rhizosphere microbiome assembly and ecosystem functioning remains poorly understood. Here, we developed a bamboo shoot-specific controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) and evaluated different urea-CRF blending ratios to identify sustainable fertilization strategy for Lei bamboo production. Mixed CRF-urea treatments outperformed both
papers.summary: This study developed a controlled-release fertilizer (CRF) for Lei bamboo and tested different blending ratios with urea to improve productivity and sustainability. Metagenomic analysis revealed that mixed CRF-urea treatments enhanced nitrogen-use efficiency and reshaped the rhizosphere microbiome, promoting beneficial microbial communities. The findings provide a sustainable fertilization strategy that balances yield with soil health.

papers.title: Genome-Resolved Metagenomics Reveals Thermophilic Microbial Diversity and Putative Hydrolase-Encoding Genes in the El Tatio Geothermal Field.
papers.abstract: Geothermal ecosystems constitute important reservoirs of thermophilic microorganisms and their associated metabolic functions; however, the genome-resolved diversity and enzymatic potential of high-altitude geothermal systems remain poorly characterized. Here, we applied shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to investigate thermophilic microbial communities inhabiting geothermal sediments from the El Tatio geothermal field, a polyextreme hydrothermal system located at ~4300 m above sea level in the Andean Altiplano of northern Chile. Genome reconstruction yielded 657 metagenome-a
papers.summary: This study used shotgun metagenomics and genome-resolved approaches to characterize the thermophilic microbial communities in sediments from the El Tatio geothermal field in the Chilean Andes, reconstructing 657 metagenome-assembled genomes. The analysis revealed significant microbial diversity and identified putative hydrolase-encoding genes, highlighting the enzymatic potential of this high-altitude geothermal ecosystem for biotechnological applications.

papers.title: De novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes with nf-core/mag.
papers.abstract: Ancient DNA provides a direct window into the evolutionary processes that have shaped living microbial species today, as well as their now extinct relatives. Advances in both sequencing methods and de novo assembly techniques have not only resulted in a flood of modern metagenomic sequencing data, but they have also allowed palaeogenomicists to retrieve vast amounts of ancient DNA from past microorganisms, including species and strains without modern reference genomes. However, the degraded nature of ancient DNA means that the standard techniques of genome assembly developed for modern DNA are
papers.summary: This paper presents nf-core/mag, a new computational pipeline for de novo assembly and authentication of ancient DNA metagenomes. It addresses the unique challenges of degraded ancient DNA, enabling researchers to reconstruct and validate genomes of past microorganisms without modern references.

papers.title: Integrated transcriptomic and hormonomic insights into cadmium tolerance of a Euglena mutabilis fungal-algal-bacterial consortium.
papers.abstract: Acidic, metal-contaminated environments harbour specialized microbial consortia adapted to extreme stress. We examined an environmental Euglena mutabilis culture naturally associated with Talaromyces and Acidiphilium acidophilum and exposed it to cadmium (Cd). Integrated transcriptomic, hormonal, structural and taxonomic analyses revealed a coordinated Cd-tolerance strategy. RNA sequencing showed differential regulation of metal transporters consistent with a shift from Cd uptake to intracellular sequestration. Transmission electron microscopy confirmed Cd compartmentalization within chloropla
papers.summary: This study characterizes a microbial consortium (Euglena mutabilis with fungal and bacterial partners) and reveals a coordinated cadmium tolerance strategy involving shifts in metal transporter expression and intracellular sequestration, as confirmed by transcriptomics and electron microscopy. The findings provide insights into how natural microbial communities adapt to heavy metal stress, with potential applications in bioremediation.

papers.title: Predicting the plastic biodegradation potential within microbial lineages and across global ecosystems.
papers.abstract: Plastic waste pollution is a global issue that threatens biodiversity and human health. Current plastic waste management practices are not sufficient to keep up with increasing plastic production rates. Microorganisms have the capacity to degrade different types of bio-based and synthetic plastics through enzymatic reactions, offering an alternative solution to traditional plastic recycling techniques. A limited number of plastic-degrading enzymes have been identified, sequenced and characterized; however, studies exploring the distribution of homologues of these enzymes across habitats and mi
papers.summary: This study predicts the potential for plastic biodegradation across microbial lineages and global ecosystems by identifying homologues of known plastic-degrading enzymes. It reveals that these enzymes are more widely distributed than previously thought, with distinct ecological niches and taxonomic patterns, offering insights into microbial strategies for plastic degradation.

papers.title: Nanopore Long-Read Metagenomics Reveals Pollution-Driven Antibiotic Resistance and Xenobiotic Degradation in Urban Beach Microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Coastal ecosystems are vital for biodiversity but are increasingly threatened by urbanisation and pollution, which significantly alter local microbial communities. This study assessed bacterial diversity and functional profiles in urban and island beaches in Belém, Brazil. Urban beaches showed significantly higher microbial diversity and evenness, alongside functional plasticity due to pollutant input, while island beaches hosted more specialised and stable communities. Taxonomic analysis revealed the significant enrichment of opportunistic genera such as Comamonas, Clostridium and Paenibacill
papers.summary: This study used nanopore long-read metagenomics to compare microbial communities between urban and island beaches in Belém, Brazil, finding that urban beaches had higher microbial diversity and functional plasticity driven by pollution, with enrichment of opportunistic genera like Comamonas, Clostridium, and Paenibacillus. The results highlight how pollution shapes antibiotic resistance and xenobiotic degradation potential in coastal microbiomes.

papers.title: 2'-FL's Depiction of the Human Physiological Function Landscape.
papers.abstract: 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) is a major fucosylated human milk oligosaccharide characterized by a terminal α1,2-linked fucose residue, which supports its interactions with gut microbes, host glycan-recognition systems, and pathogen-binding sites. This review proposes that 2'-FL acts mainly through a hierarchical host-microbiota mechanism: it first shapes gut microbial composition, then influences microbial metabolites such as short-chain fatty acids, and subsequently contributes to intestinal barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, and broader physiological outcomes. Current evidence is strongest
papers.summary: This review proposes that the human milk oligosaccharide 2'-fucosyllactose (2'-FL) acts through a hierarchical host-microbiota mechanism, first shaping gut microbial composition, then influencing microbial metabolites like short-chain fatty acids, and subsequently contributing to intestinal barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, and broader physiological outcomes. The paper maps the current evidence for 2'-FL's effects across human physiological functions, highlighting its interactions with gut microbes and host glycan-recognition systems.

papers.title: Gut Microbiota and Ischemic Stroke: From Pre-Stroke Dysbiosis and Acute-Phase Changes to Therapeutic Applications.
papers.abstract: Ischemic stroke poses a major global health burden, and growing evidence points to the microbiota-gut-brain axis as an important contributor to stroke pathophysiology and recovery. The purpose of this review is to summarize current knowledge on bidirectional gut-brain communication in stroke, establishing gut dysbiosis as an upstream risk factor for stroke onset and examining microbiota dynamics across acute and chronic phases.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current evidence on the gut-brain axis in ischemic stroke, highlighting gut dysbiosis as a risk factor for stroke onset and describing how the microbiota changes during acute and chronic phases. It also discusses potential therapeutic applications targeting the gut microbiota to improve stroke outcomes.

papers.title: Differential Quantification of Cutibacterium acnes Phylotypes IA and IB/II on Healthy and Acne-Prone Human Skin.
papers.abstract: Cutibacterium acnes is a common skin bacterium that inhabits sebaceous follicles and comprises multiple phylotypes. Healthy skin is colonized by a C. acnes population dominated by phylotypes IA, IB, and II. In acne, this diversity is reduced, with a predominance of phylotype IA. Quantifying C. acnes phylotypes has been challenging due to the lack of specific methods. Here, we developed a droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) assay that separately quantifies phylotype IA and phylotypes IB/II, based on a difference in the hyaluronidase gene. The method was applied to skin swabs from 14 healthy individuals
papers.summary: This paper describes a new droplet digital PCR (ddPCR) assay that can separately quantify Cutibacterium acnes phylotype IA and phylotypes IB/II based on a difference in the hyaluronidase gene. The method was successfully applied to skin swabs from 14 healthy individuals, providing a tool to study the microbial shifts associated with acne.

papers.title: Inonotus hispidus Polysaccharides Prepared by Graded Ethanol Precipitation Modulate the Gut-Immune Axis in Cyclophosphamide-Induced Immunosuppressed Mice.
papers.abstract: Inonotus hispidus polysaccharides (IHP) from this edible medicinal fungus exhibit notable immunological benefits, yet fraction specific effects on host immunity and the gut microbiota remain unclear. This study investigated the differential bioactivities of three graded ethanol-precipitated fractions (IHP-65, IHP-75, and IHP-85) in a cyclophosphamide (CTX)-induced immunosuppressed mouse model. Structural characterization revealed that IHP-65 was a 1098 kDa complex heteropolysaccharide, whereas IHP-85 comprised a highly uniform 19.7 kDa glucan core. Following oral administration, all fractions
papers.summary: This study shows that different ethanol-precipitated fractions of polysaccharides from the medicinal fungus Inonotus hispidus have distinct structural properties and varying abilities to restore immune function in immunosuppressed mice, likely by modulating the gut microbiota and the gut-immune axis. The findings suggest that specific polysaccharide fractions could be tailored for immunomodulatory applications.

papers.title: Multi-omics uncovers the critical role of ceramide-mediated Acinetobacter growth suppression in pressure injury healing under aging and malnutrition.
papers.abstract: The epidemiology of tolerance and susceptibility in an individual suggests that aging and malnutrition (MN) should be critically regarded as a common clinical combination in the pathomechanism of pressure ulcer/injury (PU). However, the influence of these two factors on wound healing has not been fully elucidated. In this study, we used a random forest (RF) to screen macro and laboratory indicators to compare the characteristic variables of single versus dual interventions for aging or MN. The 16S ribosomal RNA (16S rRNA) microbiome sequencing as well as serum and skin metabolomics studies wer
papers.summary: This study uses multi-omics approaches (16S rRNA microbiome sequencing, metabolomics, and random forest modeling) to investigate how aging and malnutrition together impair pressure injury healing. The findings reveal that ceramide-mediated suppression of Acinetobacter growth plays a critical role in the delayed healing process, offering new mechanistic insights into the combined effects of these two risk factors.

papers.title: Generation and Application of Ultra-Fine, Long-Term Stable Nanobubble Water: An Evaluation of Inclusion Effects on Aromatic Components and Antimicrobial Activity.
papers.abstract: Nano- and pico-bubble water (NPB), containing hydrogen or ozone, is widely used as a cleaning agent due to its bactericidal and antiviral properties. However, some products-such as certain hydrogen waters-contain only large bubbles or have an extremely low bubble count, making them sometimes indistinguishable from ordinary drinking water. To accurately evaluate NPB activity, we developed a method for producing ultra-nano-pico-bubble water (NanoGAS water [NGW]), an ultra-fine bubble water that is stable and non-volatile over extended periods. By combining a mixed gas-liquid fluid rotary mixer a
papers.summary: This study presents a method for generating ultra-fine, long-term stable nanobubble water (NanoGAS water) and evaluates its effects on aromatic components and antimicrobial activity. The findings suggest that this nanobubble water has potential applications in cleaning and preservation, with implications for food and medical industries.

papers.title: Gut microbiota of sprint athletes: signature microbes and dietary links.
papers.abstract: The gut microbiota has emerged as an important biological factor associated with host physiological status in athletes. However, relevant research remains limited for sprint athletes, whose physiological demands differ substantially from those of endurance athletes.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the gut microbiota of sprint athletes, identifying signature microbes and their associations with dietary intake, which differ from those seen in endurance athletes. The findings highlight unique microbial and dietary links in sprint athletes, expanding our understanding of the athlete-gut microbiome axis.

papers.title: Gut microbiota-derived imidazole propionate is associated with obesity.
papers.abstract: Obesity is a progressive metabolic disorder with some well-recognized markers, such as increased or elevated branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs). However, the role of gut microbiota-derived metabolites remains unknown in Asian populations. By employing an integrated multi-omics approach combining metagenomic and plasma metabolomic profiling in an Asian cohort alongside a longitudinal analysis of a bariatric surgery subgroup. We identified a distinct metabolic signature in obesity characterized by depleted circulating histidine and a concomitant elevation of Imidazole Propionate (ImP). The eleva
papers.summary: This study identifies a distinct metabolic signature in an Asian cohort with obesity, characterized by depleted circulating histidine and elevated gut microbiota-derived imidazole propionate (ImP). Using integrated metagenomic and plasma metabolomic profiling, including longitudinal analysis of a bariatric surgery subgroup, the findings suggest ImP as a potential marker linking gut microbiota to obesity.

papers.title: Ecosystem settings and urbanization shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on coastal microplastics.
papers.abstract: Coastal wetlands are increasingly contaminated by microplastics that provide long-lived substrates for microbial colonization, yet the joint effects of ecosystem settings and urbanization on plastisphere communities and their resistomes remain poorly understood. Here, we used a 2 × 2 factorial design across mangrove and sandy-beach sediments under rural and urban influence, combined with metagenomic profiling, to characterize microplastic-associated microbiota and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs). Microbial communities on microplastics showed clear separation between mangroves and sandy shor
papers.summary: This study investigates how ecosystem type (mangrove vs. sandy beach) and urbanization level (rural vs. urban) jointly shape microbial communities and antibiotic resistance genes on microplastics in coastal wetlands. Using a factorial design and metagenomic profiling, the authors found that both factors significantly influence the plastisphere microbiome and its resistome, with distinct community separation between mangroves and sandy shores.

papers.title: Effect of phosphorus fraction in shaping bacterial and archaeal community succession in the largest hydrologically connected lake of Northeast Asia.
papers.abstract: Microbial beta diversity and its components are key ecological indicators for understanding community assembly in lake sediments, yet their coupling with phosphorus (P) fractions remains poorly understood in hydrologically connected lake systems. In this study, sediment cores were collected from Xingkai Lake, the largest freshwater lake in Northeast Asia with a unique twin lake structure, and were analyzed using metagenomic sequencing combined with sequential P fractionation. Results showed that total beta diversity and species turnover for bacteria and archaea increased significantly with sed
papers.summary: This study investigates how phosphorus fractions shape bacterial and archaeal community succession in the sediments of Xingkai Lake, the largest hydrologically connected lake in Northeast Asia. Using metagenomic sequencing and sequential phosphorus fractionation, the authors found that total beta diversity and species turnover for both bacteria and archaea increased significantly with sediment depth, with phosphorus fractions playing a key role in driving community assembly.

papers.title: From natural assemblages to synthetic communities in the Lupinus microbiome.
papers.abstract: Plant roots harbour complex microbial communities that enhance nutrient acquisition, stress tolerance, and pathogen defence, yet their assembly and functional dynamics remain incompletely understood.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes current knowledge of the Lupinus root microbiome, from natural field assemblages to synthetic community approaches, highlighting how host genetics and soil conditions shape microbial assembly and function. It underscores the potential of synthetic communities to improve nutrient acquisition and stress tolerance in lupins, while identifying key knowledge gaps for future research.

papers.title: Gut microbial diversity and candidate keystone taxa in Indian tribes: Insights across lifestyle-ecological continuum and health associations.
papers.abstract: Despite the critical role of the gut microbiome in host physiology and health, it remains poorly characterized in Indigenous populations undergoing rapid acculturation. This study presents high-resolution, whole-genome metagenomic profiling of gut microbiota from five Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs) of Southern India, Irula, Jenu Kuruba, Kurumba, Chenchu, and Konda Savara, spanning distinct ecological zones and cultural transitions. Using an ecology-lifestyle continuum framework, we investigated taxonomic and functional diversity with a focus on identifying computationally inferr
papers.summary: This study provides high-resolution metagenomic profiling of gut microbiomes from five Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups in Southern India, revealing distinct taxonomic and functional diversity linked to lifestyle and ecological transitions. It identifies candidate keystone taxa and associations with health, offering insights into the gut microbiome of understudied Indigenous populations undergoing acculturation.

papers.title: Domestication shapes the gut microbial structure and metabolic function in felids: a metagenomic study of wild and domestic cats.
papers.abstract: The domestication process has profoundly altered the dietary patterns and living conditions of cats, with corresponding effects on their gut microbiome.
papers.summary: This study uses metagenomics to compare the gut microbiomes of wild and domestic cats, revealing that domestication significantly alters both the microbial community structure and its metabolic functions, likely due to changes in diet and environment.

papers.title: Glacial meltwater is associated with gene-specific diversification of metal resistance genes in high Arctic soil microbiomes.
papers.abstract: Climate warming accelerates glacial meltwater delivery to Arctic lakes, mobilizing metals from thawing catchments and reshaping the selective landscape experienced by resident microbes. Whether these gradients leave detectable signatures of diversification in environmental resistance genes remains unclear. We investigated four metal resistance genes (merA, arsC, cadA, and chrR) in metagenomic datasets from Lake Hazen (Nunavut, Canada), the largest High Arctic freshwater lake, sampled across a natural hydrological gradient of Control, Low-runoff, and High-runoff regimes. Using a space-for-time
papers.summary: This study examines how glacial meltwater runoff in the High Arctic influences the diversification of metal resistance genes in soil microbiomes. By analyzing metagenomic data from Lake Hazen across a hydrological gradient, the authors found that increased meltwater runoff is associated with gene-specific diversification of mercury, arsenic, cadmium, and chromium resistance genes, suggesting that climate-driven environmental changes are shaping microbial adaptation.

papers.title: Dietary sulforaphane in cancer chemoprevention: epigenetic regulation and PRMT5-MEP50 complex inhibition-a systematic review.
papers.abstract: Cancer chemoprevention using dietary bioactive compounds has emerged as a promising, cost-effective strategy to reduce global cancer incidence and mortality. Sulforaphane (SFN), an isothiocyanate abundant in cruciferous vegetables, has attracted considerable attention for its pleiotropic anticancer effects.
papers.summary: This systematic review examines how dietary sulforaphane (SFN), a compound found in cruciferous vegetables, exerts chemopreventive effects against cancer. The authors highlight SFN's dual mechanisms: epigenetic regulation (e.g., histone modifications) and inhibition of the PRMT5-MEP50 complex, which is implicated in cancer progression. The review consolidates evidence supporting SFN as a promising dietary strategy for cancer prevention.

papers.title: Effects of probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics on lung function and symptoms in adults with bronchial asthma: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics may exert beneficial effects on asthma by modulating the gut microbiota and the "gut-lung axis". However, no systematic review or meta-analysis has specifically focused on adult asthma patients.
papers.summary: This systematic review and meta-analysis evaluates the effects of probiotics, prebiotics, and synbiotics on lung function and symptoms in adults with bronchial asthma, focusing on the gut-lung axis. It finds that these interventions may offer some benefit, though the evidence is limited and warrants further research.

papers.title: From Gut to Brain: Probiotics as an Emerging Adjunctive Strategy for Insomnia and Sleep Disturbances.
papers.abstract: Too little sleep and incidental insomnia are two common conditions in which sleep is disrupted. Insomnia is often accompanied by emotional, metabolic, and immunological deterioration. The purpose of this narrative review is to better understand the gut-brain axis and evaluate the potential usefulness of probiotics in the treatment of insomnia and related sleep problems.
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the gut-brain axis and evaluates the potential of probiotics as an adjunctive treatment for insomnia and sleep disturbances. It synthesizes current evidence suggesting that modulating the gut microbiome may improve sleep quality and associated emotional, metabolic, and immunological symptoms.

papers.title: Integrative analysis of gut microbiota, plasma metabolome, and gene expression identifies causal mediators in Graves' disease pathogenesis.
papers.abstract: Graves' disease (GD) is characterized by hyperthyroidism and is influenced by genetic and environmental factors. The "gut-thyroid axis" establishes a connection between the gut microbiota and GD, yet the underlying potential mechanisms remain unclear. This study employed Mendelian randomization to investigate the causal relationships between the gut microbiota and GD, aiming to identify key microbial taxa and their metabolites, as well as to explore the regulatory roles of relevant genes in the pathogenesis of GD.
papers.summary: This study uses Mendelian randomization to investigate causal links between gut microbiota and Graves' disease, identifying specific microbial taxa and their metabolites as potential mediators. It also explores gene expression regulatory roles, providing new insights into the gut-thyroid axis in GD pathogenesis.

papers.title: Integrating tongue coating microbiome, tongue coating metabolomics, and exhaled breath metabolomics via machine learning to identify chronic atrophic gastritis.
papers.abstract: Chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG) is a precancerous gastric condition with limited non-invasive diagnostic options. Alterations in the oral microbiome and its localized metabolic profiles may provide early multi-omics signatures of disease progression.
papers.summary: This study integrates tongue coating microbiome, tongue coating metabolomics, and exhaled breath metabolomics using machine learning to identify non-invasive biomarkers for chronic atrophic gastritis (CAG), a precancerous gastric condition. The multi-omics approach reveals distinct microbial and metabolic alterations associated with CAG, offering a promising diagnostic strategy that could reduce reliance on invasive endoscopy.

papers.title: Persistent gut microbiota dysbiosis and metabolic remodeling after ceftriaxone exposure in mice: a cross-study re-analysis.
papers.abstract: Broad-spectrum antibiotics are known to disrupt the gut microbial environment, which can lead to sustained physiological consequences. Ceftriaxone (CTX) is a β-lactam antibiotic widely used in neuroscience research to enhance expression of the glutamate transporter GLT-1, a key regulator of excitatory neurotransmission in the brain. However, CTX also induces marked alterations in gut microbial composition, yet the consistency and functional consequences of these changes across studies remain poorly defined.
papers.journal: Frontiers in cellular and infection microbiology
papers.summary: This study re-analyzed existing datasets to assess the consistency of gut microbiota changes after ceftriaxone treatment in mice, finding persistent dysbiosis and metabolic remodeling across studies. The results highlight that ceftriaxone's effects on the gut microbiome are reproducible and may have functional consequences beyond its neurological applications.

papers.title: Methodological bias shapes the interpretation of the urinary microbiome in low-biomass systems.
papers.abstract: The recognition of the urinary microbiome (urobiome) has challenged the long-standing paradigm of urinary tract sterility, revealing diverse microbial communities associated with both urinary health and disease. However, the characterization of the urobiome remains highly variable across studies, particularly due to the low-biomass nature of urine samples and the strong influence of methodological bias. In this Mini Review, we examine how factors such as sample collection methods, contamination dynamics, DNA extraction protocols, sequencing approaches, and bioinformatic pipelines shape microbi
papers.summary: This mini-review highlights how methodological choices—from sample collection and DNA extraction to sequencing and bioinformatic analysis—can significantly bias the characterization of the low-biomass urinary microbiome, leading to inconsistent findings across studies. The authors emphasize the need for standardized protocols to improve reproducibility and accurate interpretation of urobiome data.

papers.title: Integrative bioinformatics analysis identifies gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated immune candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to identify and prioritize gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated host candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis (PBC) through integrative multi-omics analysis and external validation.
papers.summary: This study uses integrative multi-omics analysis to identify gut microbiota-derived metabolite-associated immune candidate targets in high-risk primary biliary cholangitis (PBC), with external validation. The findings highlight potential host targets that may link the gut microbiome to PBC pathogenesis, offering new avenues for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: Community Dynamics in a Changing World: highlights from the 1st Puerto Rico & Caribbean Microbiome Symposium and vision for a new microbiome hub.
papers.abstract: The Puerto Rico Center for Microbiome Sciences (PR-CMS) seeks to become a leading hub for multiomics research and host-microbiota symbiosis in the Caribbean. As part of this effort, PR-CMS organizes an annual symposium that convenes international leaders, regional experts, and the local scientific community to address key challenges in microbiome science. The 1st Microbiome Symposium of Puerto Rico and the Caribbean, titled "Community Dynamics in a Changing World," took place in San Juan in February 2026. The event brought together more than 200 participants, including researchers, trainees, a
papers.summary: This report summarizes the first Puerto Rico & Caribbean Microbiome Symposium, highlighting efforts to establish a regional hub for microbiome and multiomics research. The event convened over 200 participants to address key challenges in microbiome science, emphasizing community dynamics and host-microbiota symbiosis in the Caribbean.

papers.title: Atopic dermatitis: pathogenesis, immunology, microbiome, and salivary biomarkers.
papers.abstract: Atopic dermatitis is a chronic inflammatory skin disease influenced by genetic predisposition, immune dysregulation, and environmental factors, as well as skin and gut microbiota. This review summarises the key mechanisms involved in this disease development, including disturbances in innate and adaptive immune responses, ethnic differences in immune pathways, and the contribution of microbial imbalance to skin barrier dysfunction. Special attention is given to salivary biomarkers-such as cortisol, melatonin, alpha-amylase, chromogranin A, C-reactive protein, and immunoglobulin A-which offer a
papers.summary: This review summarizes the pathogenesis of atopic dermatitis, focusing on immune dysregulation, genetic and environmental factors, and the role of skin and gut microbiota in skin barrier dysfunction. It highlights salivary biomarkers such as cortisol, melatonin, and immunoglobulin A as a non-invasive diagnostic tool, though their clinical utility requires further validation.

papers.title: Placental and maternal microbiome adaptations in a preeclamptic-like mouse model.
papers.abstract: The maternal microbiome plays a crucial role in pregnancy with growing evidence supporting vertical microbial transmission from mother to fetus. The placenta, once considered sterile, may serve as a conduit for this transfer. We hypothesized that the placental microbial signatures would be distinctly different from oral, fecal, or vaginal microbiomes in pregnant mice.
papers.summary: This study characterizes the placental microbiome in a preeclamptic-like mouse model and compares it to maternal oral, fecal, and vaginal microbiomes, finding distinct microbial signatures in the placenta. The results support the idea that the placenta is not sterile and may play a role in maternal-fetal microbial transfer, with adaptations occurring under preeclampsia-like conditions.

papers.title: Baseline characteristics of the HOMINY (human papillomavirus, human immunodeficiency virus, and oral microbiota interplay in Nigerian youth) prospective longitudinal cohort.
papers.abstract: The HOMINY (Human Papillomavirus, Human Immunodeficiency Virus, and Oral Microbiota Interplay in Nigerian Youth) cohort is a prospective longitudinal study established to investigate oral HPV infection and the oral microbiome among mother-child pairs with and without HIV in Nigeria. The objective of this analysis was to describe baseline demographic and clinical characteristics of the cohort, including HPV awareness, HPV vaccination, and cervical cancer screening practice by HIV status.
papers.summary: This paper describes the baseline characteristics of the HOMINY cohort, a prospective longitudinal study in Nigeria examining oral HPV infection and the oral microbiome in mother-child pairs with and without HIV. The analysis reports demographic and clinical data, including HPV awareness, vaccination, and cervical cancer screening practices, stratified by HIV status.

papers.title: Paper mulberry in animal nutrition: processing, host responses, and product quality.
papers.abstract: Paper mulberry (Broussonetia papyrifera) has attracted increasing attention as a local feed resource because it combines perennial woody biomass, protein-rich foliage and diverse plant secondary compounds. Its feeding value depends on plant part, harvest stage, processing method, fermentation quality, target animal species and dietary inclusion level. This review examines paper mulberry from feed composition and processing to animal responses, product traits and proposed mechanisms. Current evidence is strongest in ruminants, where paper mulberry silage or fermented feed has been associated wi
papers.summary: This review examines the use of paper mulberry (Broussonetia papyrifera) as a feed resource for livestock, covering its nutritional composition, processing methods, and effects on animal performance and product quality. The evidence is strongest in ruminants, where fermented or silage forms show promise, but outcomes vary by plant part, harvest stage, and inclusion level.
